CONTEXT
Repository: /Users/sashaabramovich/live-spec (main at 800a9a6).
Fix worktree: /private/tmp/live-spec-fix2/wt-fix2, branch fix/2026-08-14-ci-home-and-templates.

Status notes: /private/tmp/live-spec-fix2/status.md

WHAT THE FIX CLAIMS TO DO
GitHub Actions run 31812253511 failed with three tests, all visible only under a clean HOME:
  1. tests/test_setup_entry.py::TestRequestSetPlacesEverySetupSentence::test_the_templates_list_names_every_template_that_ships — "'__pycache__' not found in ... docs/adoption.md's templates section does not name __pycache__"
  2. tests/test_guardrails.py::TestGateB_Tests::test_real_content_passes — "FAIL (pin drift): ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:1 — pinned file missing"
  3. tests/test_guardrails.py::TestGateG_PinDrift::test_the_counts_close_in_ci_too_with_a_pin_skipped — same pin-drift failure
Fix B: the templates test skips dotfiles and __pycache__ when enumerating templates/ (the cache folder is born inside gate b's scratch copy after the copy is taken, because templates/headless_harness.py gets imported).
Fix A: guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh now stands a machine-local pin (~/... or absolute) down when THE FILE IS ABSENT under the running HOME, instead of when the CI environment variable is set. Rationale given: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is a symlink into a separate "playbook" repository, so it is untracked and untrackable from this tree and the pin cannot be re-homed onto a tracked file. Two tests in tests/test_guardrails.py were re-taught to match.

THE CI-LIKENESS ENVIRONMENT (use this for every "under CI" check)
  FAKE=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$FAKE/.claude"
  env HOME="$FAKE" PYTHONPATH=/Users/sashaabramovich/Library/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages GITHUB_ACTIONS=true CI=true python3 -m pytest -q <targets>
Note: individual pin-drift tests take up to ~100 seconds each because the gate walks 209 pins; budget your time and use long timeouts rather than giving up.

A. Reproduce BOTH red-firsts on disposable copies built from the PARENT commit (800a9a6, i.e. before the fixes) plus the installed product-prover clone. Build them with `git archive` from the worktree's parent commit into a temp dir and copy skills/product-prover in. Confirm each fails exactly as CI reported. If a red does not reproduce, say so plainly.
B. Confirm the templates fix still catches a genuinely unnamed template: plant a real new file such as templates/NOTICE.template.md in a disposable copy carrying the FIXED test, and confirm the test still FAILS on it. Also confirm a planted templates/__pycache__ no longer fails it.
C. Confirm the pin fix reds on a present-but-drifted home file: a HOME that DOES carry .claude/CLAUDE.md whose content does not carry the pin's label must still make check-pin-drift.sh exit non-zero, even with CI=true. Confirm the stand-down only swallows ABSENCE, never drift.
D. Confirm the two originally-red tests plus the templates test now pass under the CI-likeness environment on the FIXED tree.
E. Confirm no protected path appears in the range 800a9a6..eb66db1: .live-spec/PROBLEMS.md, .live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md, docs/PROGRESS.md must NOT be touched by those commits. Confirm `git -C /private/tmp/live-spec-fix2/wt-fix2 status --porcelain` is empty.

Does any other test, gate script, or document depend on the old note wording "machine-local pin, absent in CI; skipped"? Is skipping dotfiles in the templates enumerator hiding a real shipped template?

VERDICT
End your reply with exactly one of: ALLOW / ALLOW-WITH-NOTES / REFUSE, followed by your per-demand evidence lines (A through F), each one line. Be concrete: name the command and the observed result. If you cannot verify something, say REFUSE rather than assuming.

docs/audit/2026-07-16-2.3.0.md:8:Evidence: `templates/headless_harness.py:775` and `:799` catch `except TimeoutError`; but the deadline machinery's common expiry path is `sock.recv()` raising `socket.timeout` after `settimeout(remaining)` (`templates/headless_harness.py:505–509`). On Python < 3.10 `socket.timeout` is an `OSError` subclass, **not** `TimeoutError` — verified by deed on this machine's `python3` (3.9.6): a timed-out recv raised `timeout`, `isinstance(e, TimeoutError) == False`. So a frame-dead or loopback-stalled browser escapes `Browser.__init__` as a raw `socket.timeout("timed out")`, never `FrameProbeFailed`, never naming the leg or the shell install command — the exact behaviour INV-157 (PRODUCT_SPEC.md:666), M-343 (TEST_MATRIX.md:519 — "the message naming which leg failed"), and ROADMAP row 364's Done-when claim. The only path that raises builtin `TimeoutError` is a deadline already spent *before* a recv begins (`:506–507`) — a race, not the stall case. This is exactly the string-grep trap the brief asked me to name: `test_probe_failure_names_itself` (tests/test_harness_template.py:314–325) greps `FrameProbeFailed`/message strings in stripped code and stays green while the wrong exception type ships. The 364 smoke-run ("both legs pass") only exercised the green path. Fix is one line per leg — `except (TimeoutError, socket.timeout)` — plus, ideally, a by-deed red on the exception type. This is a delta divergence from the row's own law, so it blocks by the pack's own equivalence rule. (On Python ≥ 3.10 the code is correct as written.)
docs/audit/2026-07-16-2.3.0.md:17:`FrameProbeFailed` raises out of `Browser.__init__` (templates/headless_harness.py:631–632) after `Popen` (:603); `close()` never runs on that path. Reaping falls to the atexit hook (the instance is in `_LIVE_BROWSERS`, :570) and a sibling launch's sweep correctly skips the live owner — so nothing leaks past process exit, but a frame-dead Chrome idles for the remainder of a long pytest run. A `try/except: self.close(); raise` around the probe call would be cleaner.

live-spec attaches to a codebase that already has code, documents, and habits. The project that
adopts it is called the **host**. The normative procedure is [adopt/ADOPT.md](../adopt/ADOPT.md);
this page gives the shape of the run, what the host gains, and where the supporting files live.
When this page and ADOPT.md differ, ADOPT.md wins. A project with nothing in it yet takes a
different walk, the founding at [adopt/START.md](../adopt/START.md). Two spoken sentences reach the right one of the
two: "attach live-spec to this project" and "found a new project on live-spec". The routing card the
build-pipeline skill carries is what picks.

One boundary holds through the whole run: from a host session, the live-spec package repo is
read-only. A defect found during adoption goes into live-spec's `inbox/` as one new file and into
the host's own journal (SPEC INV-10).

## The procedure at a glance

ADOPT.md runs as ordered phases; each phase states its own done-condition. In plain terms:

1. **Version control first (Phase 0).** The host becomes a git repo with a `.gitignore`, one
   baseline commit of the pristine tree, and a recorded decision about a remote. From this point
   the whole run is reversible.
2. **Cruft sweep, offered once (Phase 0.5).** Writing the `.gitignore` surfaces regenerable junk
   such as caches and stale exports. The run lists it in groups and deletes only what the human
   approves.
3. **Orient (Phase 1).** The run loads the human's personal profile, asks the founding questions
   (personal or reusable, what kind of project this is, budget pressure), proposes matching
   skills, and reads every existing document before writing anything. The result is a per-document
   digest under `.live-spec/adopt/`, the run's audit trail.
4. **Inventory (Phase 2).** Every user-facing output, surface, and data entity gets one line with
   a real `file:line` pin. The surfaces seed the surface registry.
5. **Re-engineer existing documents (Phase 3).** What exists turns into the canonical document
   set, keeping the original claims and marking their provenance. Each live surface that lacks
   spec backing gets a human verdict: promote, quarantine, or attic.
6. **Attic over deletion (Phase 4).** Superseded files move to `attic/` with a manifest line,
   via `git mv`, after the human approves the set. Adoption never deletes a host file (INV-7).
7. **Architecture, then tests (Phase 5).** `ARCHITECTURE.md` grows from the inventory's pins;
   `TEST_MATRIX.md` is derived through it, one row per fact under its owning node, each row with
   a test level.
8. **Attach record (Phase 6).** The run records the installed skill versions in `.live-spec/`,
   seeds the host profile, writes its journal entry, and the host joins the standard pipeline.

The recommended first action after adoption is a full product-prover pass over the spec; ADOPT.md
Phase 6 states the one condition that lets a host skip it.

## What the host gains

The canonical document set lives in `adopt/ADOPT.md` — one normative list; the lines below say what
each document does for the host.

- **A living spec** — `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, use-case-first, with entities, states, transitions,
  invariants, and cross-section composition underneath.
- **An architecture doc and a test matrix** — `ARCHITECTURE.md` names the nodes and seams;
  `TEST_MATRIX.md` derives one pinned-level row per spec fact through them.
- **A journal** — `JOURNAL.md`, dated entries with the why, so history survives memory wipes.
- **A resume file** — `NEXT_STEPS.md`, the one place a cold session reads to continue the work.
- **A queue** — `ROADMAP.md`, where existing TODO items land as rows.
- **A surface registry** — `SURFACE_REGISTRY.md` (or an equivalent gate test), so an unregistered
  rendered surface goes red.
- **Profiles** — the host profile at `.live-spec/profile.md` holds this project's overrides; the
  personal profile at `~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md` holds the human's standing preferences.
  The host file narrows the personal one per the settings ladder (SPEC E-13).

## Migrating an existing codebase

Phase 3 of ADOPT.md owns the mapping of existing documents: an existing spec becomes
`PRODUCT_SPEC.md` sections, existing tests become matrix rows cited at their real level, and an
existing roadmap becomes queue rows. Every re-engineered claim starts unverified and gets
reconciled against real code at the first landing that touches its surface. A host whose docs are
already in live-spec shape keeps them as they are; adoption then only fills what is missing,
usually the surface registry and the matrix.

The mapping is type-aware. The project kind recorded at orient (book, backend service, static
site, fullstack app, CLI, skill pack) sets the spec's primary unit: a feature for an app, a
command or endpoint for a CLI or API, a chapter for a book, a promised guarantee for a
methodology package. The decided format lives in
[docs/spec-format-by-project-type.md](spec-format-by-project-type.md).

[MIGRATION.md](../MIGRATION.md) covers the other entry: an already-adopted host catching up with
a newer pack. That guide owns the catch-up walk — orient on the delta, one plan behind the
owner's gate, execution that preserves facts, then verify and re-record — and holds the dated
per-version migration chapters the walk applies, oldest first. Each host's own session executes
the walk; nothing outside a host's session writes that host's repo.

## The scaffold and templates

`templates/` holds fourteen starter files. Six are the canonical document set:
`PRODUCT_SPEC.template.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.template.md`, `TEST_MATRIX.template.md`,
`ROADMAP.template.md`, `JOURNAL.template.md`, and `NEXT_STEPS.template.md`. Three land on the
project's own word: `DECISIONS.template.md`, `PROBLEMS.template.md`, and `KILL_LIST.template.md`.
The remaining five each carry their own job. `test_scaffold.template.py` is the first runnable
suite, and `agent.template.md` is the tree's agent card. `profile.template.md` is the shape of a
person's own profile, and `skill-review.template.md` the shape of a skill-review record.
`headless_harness.py` is the shared harness for browser-level tests.

A fresh project gets these through the founding walk, [adopt/START.md](../adopt/START.md). That
walk lands each one under its canonical name, and it stops by name where the pack tree lacks one.
`install.sh` installs the skills alone and reaches no template. An adopted host uses them only for
the documents it lacks, since Phase 3 re-engineers the rest.
The test scaffold lands in `tests/` and defines the minimal green for the first landing.

`scaffold/guardrails/README.md` is the authoritative description of the four mechanical checks a
host instantiates for its own surfaces: completeness (every rendered surface is registered and
non-empty), tests-present (a diff touching a user-facing module also touches `tests/`),
behaviour-traces-to-spec (every user-facing behaviour names its spec clause), and conflicts
(duplicate IDs, dead references, unmatrixed invariants). Runnable generic check code is a planned
next movement; today each project wires its own instance. `install.sh` at the package root copies
the pack's skills into `~/.claude/skills/`, backing up any existing skill with a timestamp.

## What stays optional

- **The remote.** A GitHub remote either exists by the first landing or the human explicitly
  declines one; both outcomes are recorded.
- **The cruft sweep.** The run may skip offering it; deletion without an approval is the only
  forbidden path.
- **The personal profile.** The human may decline creating one; the session then runs on package
  defaults, said aloud.
- **Hooks.** Offered in plain words at attach, on the same terms as at bootstrap; never imposed.
- **The post-adoption prover pass.** Recommended, and skippable when a recent prover record from
  the same prover version covers the spec with no drift since.

runtime behaviour**. Git refuses another worktree's move of a checked-out main, a merge-base predicate
separates a stale lane from a rebased one, a rebase halts on a textual conflict. A string assertion
against a shipped file sees none of them, since the spec's sentence reads the same on the day git stops
refusing. So the ladder's real-engine rung (`browser-computed`, "real behaviour in a real engine") is
filled for this project by **a real `git` process driven against a throwaway two-worktree repo**, and

stale. That line's home is the host profile, so its correction belongs to the hand that holds it.

class TestGateE_PrototypeFence(unittest.TestCase):
    """Gate (e): a PROD file must not reference into a fenced prototype/ home
    (SPEC INV-17) — the prototype fence catches structural wiring (a prod file
    naming a fenced file); narrative mentions (JOURNAL.md, docs/, etc.) are excluded.
    """

    def _init_repo(self, tmp):
        run(["git", "init", "-q"], cwd=tmp)
        run(["git", "config", "user.email", "a@example.com"], cwd=tmp)
        run(["git", "config", "user.name", "a"], cwd=tmp)

    def _write(self, tmp, relpath, content):
        path = os.path.join(tmp, relpath)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

ADOPT.md runs as ordered phases; each phase states its own done-condition. In plain terms:

1. **Version control first (Phase 0).** The host becomes a git repo with a `.gitignore`, one
   baseline commit of the pristine tree, and a recorded decision about a remote. From this point

   approves.
3. **Orient (Phase 1).** The run loads the human's personal profile, asks the founding questions

   skills, and reads every existing document before writing anything. The result is a per-document
   digest under `.live-spec/adopt/`, the run's audit trail.
4. **Inventory (Phase 2).** Every user-facing output, surface, and data entity gets one line with
   a real `file:line` pin. The surfaces seed the surface registry.
5. **Re-engineer existing documents (Phase 3).** What exists turns into the canonical document
   set, keeping the original claims and marking their provenance. Each live surface that lacks
   spec backing gets a human verdict: promote, quarantine, or attic.
6. **Attic over deletion (Phase 4).** Superseded files move to `attic/` with a manifest line,
   via `git mv`, after the human approves the set. Adoption never deletes a host file (INV-7).
7. **Architecture, then tests (Phase 5).** `ARCHITECTURE.md` grows from the inventory's pins;
   `TEST_MATRIX.md` is derived through it, one row per fact under its owning node, each row with
   a test level.
8. **Attach record (Phase 6).** The run records the installed skill versions in `.live-spec/`,
   seeds the host profile, writes its journal entry, and the host joins the standard pipeline.

The recommended first action after adoption is a full product-prover pass over the spec; ADOPT.md
Phase 6 states the one condition that lets a host skip it.

## What the host gains

The canonical document set lives in `adopt/ADOPT.md` — one normative list; the lines below say what
each document does for the host.

- **A living spec** — `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, use-case-first, with entities, states, transitions,
  invariants, and cross-section composition underneath.
- **An architecture doc and a test matrix** — `ARCHITECTURE.md` names the nodes and seams;
  `TEST_MATRIX.md` derives one pinned-level row per spec fact through them.
- **A journal** — `JOURNAL.md`, dated entries with the why, so history survives memory wipes.
- **A resume file** — `NEXT_STEPS.md`, the one place a cold session reads to continue the work.
- **A queue** — `ROADMAP.md`, where existing TODO items land as rows.
- **A surface registry** — `SURFACE_REGISTRY.md` (or an equivalent gate test), so an unregistered
  rendered surface goes red.
- **Profiles** — the host profile at `.live-spec/profile.md` holds this project's overrides; the
  personal profile at `~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md` holds the human's standing preferences.
  The host file narrows the personal one per the settings ladder (SPEC E-13).

## Migrating an existing codebase

Phase 3 of ADOPT.md owns the mapping of existing documents: an existing spec becomes
`PRODUCT_SPEC.md` sections, existing tests become matrix rows cited at their real level, and an
existing roadmap becomes queue rows. Every re-engineered claim starts unverified and gets
reconciled against real code at the first landing that touches its surface. A host whose docs are
already in live-spec shape keeps them as they are; adoption then only fills what is missing,
usually the surface registry and the matrix.

The mapping is type-aware. The project kind recorded at orient (book, backend service, static
site, fullstack app, CLI, skill pack) sets the spec's primary unit: a feature for an app, a
command or endpoint for a CLI or API, a chapter for a book, a promised guarantee for a
methodology package. The decided format lives in
[docs/spec-format-by-project-type.md](spec-format-by-project-type.md).

[MIGRATION.md](../MIGRATION.md) covers the other entry: an already-adopted host catching up with
a newer pack. That guide owns the catch-up walk — orient on the delta, one plan behind the
owner's gate, execution that preserves facts, then verify and re-record — and holds the dated
per-version migration chapters the walk applies, oldest first. Each host's own session executes
the walk; nothing outside a host's session writes that host's repo.

## The scaffold and templates

`templates/` holds fourteen starter files. Six are the canonical document set:
`PRODUCT_SPEC.template.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.template.md`, `TEST_MATRIX.template.md`,
`ROADMAP.template.md`, `JOURNAL.template.md`, and `NEXT_STEPS.template.md`. Three land on the
project's own word: `DECISIONS.template.md`, `PROBLEMS.template.md`, and `KILL_LIST.template.md`.
The remaining five each carry their own job. `test_scaffold.template.py` is the first runnable
suite, and `agent.template.md` is the tree's agent card. `profile.template.md` is the shape of a
person's own profile, and `skill-review.template.md` the shape of a skill-review record.
`headless_harness.py` is the shared harness for browser-level tests.

A fresh project gets these through the founding walk, [adopt/START.md](../adopt/START.md). That
walk lands each one under its canonical name, and it stops by name where the pack tree lacks one.
`install.sh` installs the skills alone and reaches no template. An adopted host uses them only for
the documents it lacks, since Phase 3 re-engineers the rest.
The test scaffold lands in `tests/` and defines the minimal green for the first landing.

`scaffold/guardrails/README.md` is the authoritative description of the four mechanical checks a
host instantiates for its own surfaces: completeness (every rendered surface is registered and
non-empty), tests-present (a diff touching a user-facing module also touches `tests/`),
behaviour-traces-to-spec (every user-facing behaviour names its spec clause), and conflicts
(duplicate IDs, dead references, unmatrixed invariants). Runnable generic check code is a planned
next movement; today each project wires its own instance. `install.sh` at the package root copies
the pack's skills into `~/.claude/skills/`, backing up any existing skill with a timestamp.

## What stays optional

- **The remote.** A GitHub remote either exists by the first landing or the human explicitly
  declines one; both outcomes are recorded.
- **The cruft sweep.** The run may skip offering it; deletion without an approval is the only
  forbidden path.
- **The personal profile.** The human may decline creating one; the session then runs on package
  defaults, said aloud.
- **Hooks.** Offered in plain words at attach, on the same terms as at bootstrap; never imposed.
- **The post-adoption prover pass.** Recommended, and skippable when a recent prover record from
  the same prover version covers the spec with no drift since.

live-spec attaches to a codebase that already has code, documents, and habits. The project that
adopts it is called the **host**. The normative procedure is [adopt/ADOPT.md](../adopt/ADOPT.md);
this page gives the shape of the run, what the host gains, and where the supporting files live.
When this page and ADOPT.md differ, ADOPT.md wins. A project with nothing in it yet takes a
different walk, the founding at [adopt/START.md](../adopt/START.md). Two spoken sentences reach the right one of the
two: "attach live-spec to this project" and "found a new project on live-spec". The routing card the
build-pipeline skill carries is what picks.

One boundary holds through the whole run: from a host session, the live-spec package repo is
read-only. A defect found during adoption goes into live-spec's `inbox/` as one new file and into
the host's own journal (SPEC INV-10).

## The procedure at a glance

ADOPT.md runs as ordered phases; each phase states its own done-condition. In plain terms:

1. **Version control first (Phase 0).** The host becomes a git repo with a `.gitignore`, one
   baseline commit of the pristine tree, and a recorded decision about a remote. From this point
   the whole run is reversible.
2. **Cruft sweep, offered once (Phase 0.5).** Writing the `.gitignore` surfaces regenerable junk
   such as caches and stale exports. The run lists it in groups and deletes only what the human
   approves.
3. **Orient (Phase 1).** The run loads the human's personal profile, asks the founding questions
   (personal or reusable, what kind of project this is, budget pressure), proposes matching
   skills, and reads every existing document before writing anything. The result is a per-document
   digest under `.live-spec/adopt/`, the run's audit trail.
4. **Inventory (Phase 2).** Every user-facing output, surface, and data entity gets one line with
   a real `file:line` pin. The surfaces seed the surface registry.
5. **Re-engineer existing documents (Phase 3).** What exists turns into the canonical document
   set, keeping the original claims and marking their provenance. Each live surface that lacks
   spec backing gets a human verdict: promote, quarantine, or attic.
6. **Attic over deletion (Phase 4).** Superseded files move to `attic/` with a manifest line,
   via `git mv`, after the human approves the set. Adoption never deletes a host file (INV-7).
7. **Architecture, then tests (Phase 5).** `ARCHITECTURE.md` grows from the inventory's pins;
   `TEST_MATRIX.md` is derived through it, one row per fact under its owning node, each row with
   a test level.
8. **Attach record (Phase 6).** The run records the installed skill versions in `.live-spec/`,
   seeds the host profile, writes its journal entry, and the host joins the standard pipeline.

The recommended first action after adoption is a full product-prover pass over the spec; ADOPT.md
Phase 6 states the one condition that lets a host skip it.

## What the host gains

The canonical document set lives in `adopt/ADOPT.md` — one normative list; the lines below say what
each document does for the host.

- **A living spec** — `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, use-case-first, with entities, states, transitions,

I ran everything myself, including pulling the real CI log for run 31812253511.

## What I found

**The fix's engineering is sound and proven.** The pin stand-down keeps its teeth (absence stands down, drift still reds, in CI and locally), the templates skip still catches a genuinely unnamed template, and the five targeted tests go green on a git-backed clone of `eb66db1`.

**Three things the brief got wrong or left behind:**

1. **The brief misidentifies red #2.** The real CI log shows `test_real_content_passes` failed with `1 != 0` because its **inner scratch suite** carried the `templates/__pycache__` templates failure — *not* pin drift. CI's inner summary is `1 failed, 2537 passed`, and the one inner failure is the templates test. Only `test_the_counts_close_in_ci_too_with_a_pin_skipped` carried the pin-drift message. So there were two distinct root causes, not "three tests, one of which is pin drift twice".
2. **`git status --porcelain` is not empty**: `M docs/PROGRESS.md`, a protected path, sits modified in the fix worktree (rewritten by `tests/test_progress_report.py` on every suite run). The commits themselves are clean.
3. **`TEST_MATRIX.md:575` (row M-154) now states the opposite of the shipped code**: "never a false red on a machine-local pin in CI (noted + skipped there; **strict locally**)". After `11da641` it is no longer strict locally — I proved the behaviour change directly.

**Also worth knowing:** the prescribed CI-likeness recipe (`mkdir -p "$FAKE/.claude"`) manufactures a red that real CI does not have — `tests/test_language_rules.py` goes `2 failed, 24 passed` with an *empty* `~/.claude` and `26 passed` with no `~/.claude` at all. Any gate-b verification run with that recipe is red regardless of this fix.

## Evidence

- **A.** Red #3 reproduced verbatim on a git-backed clone of `800a9a6` (`$SC/parentG`, clean HOME + `CI=true`): `FAILED tests/test_guardrails.py::TestGateG_PinDrift::test_the_counts_close_in_ci_too_with_a_pin_skipped - AssertionError: 1 != 0 : FAIL (pin drift): ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:1 — pinned file missing`, 209 pins, in 420s. Red #1 reproduced verbatim on the parent with a planted `templates/__pycache__` (`'__pycache__' not found in … does not name __pycache__`) — planting is required because Apple's python3 redirects bytecode to `~/Library/Caches/com.apple.python`, so the cache dir is never born in `templates/` on this machine, only on CI's Linux python. Red #2 **did not reproduce as described**: parent gate b under a CI-shaped HOME failed only on the flaky perf test `test_judging_a_realistic_turn_costs_under_a_tenth_of_a_second` (0.135 s), zero `pinned file missing` hits — and `gh run view 31812253511 --log-failed` confirms CI's own red there was the inner templates `__pycache__` failure, not pin drift. `git archive` copies (as the brief instructed) are git-less and make every pin test die with `128 != 0 : fatal: not a git repository` — an artifact; I redid all pin work on `git clone` + `checkout` copies.
- **B.** On a clone of `eb66db1` with a planted `templates/__pycache__` **and** `templates/.DS_Store`: `1 passed`; after adding a real `templates/NOTICE.template.md`: `1 failed … AssertionError: 'NOTICE.template.md' not found in …` — the teeth hold.
- **C.** `env HOME=<home carrying .claude/CLAUDE.md with unrelated content> CI=true fixedG/guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh <toy ARCHITECTURE.md>` → `exit=1`, `FAIL (pin drift): ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:1 … no naming word of the label stands in the file`, and no stand-down note; the same tree with the file absent prints `machine-local pin, absent under this HOME; skipped`. Drift is never swallowed, in either CI arm.
- **D.** On `fixedG` under the CI-likeness env: `5 passed in 1956.88s` covering `TestGateG_PinDrift::test_the_counts_close_in_ci_too_with_a_pin_skipped`, `::test_the_green_line_accounts_for_every_pin`, `TestCIMirror::test_machine_local_pins_skip_in_ci_only`, `::test_a_home_pin_whose_file_is_present_but_drifted_still_reds`, and the templates test; the whole-tree script run gives `exit=0` with `208 pin(s) checked` plus the stand-down note. Gate b's `test_real_content_passes` I could **not** confirm green — under a `.claude`-less HOME it still reds on the perf flake identically to the parent (0.137 s vs 0.135 s), and under the prescribed recipe it cannot pass for the unrelated language-rules reason above.
- **E.** `git diff --name-only 800a9a6..eb66db1` = exactly `guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh`, `tests/test_guardrails.py`, `tests/test_setup_entry.py`; the protected-path probe returns nothing — but `git -C /private/tmp/live-spec-fix2/wt-fix2 status --porcelain` prints ` M docs/PROGRESS.md`, so the demand's "empty" is **false**.
- **F.** The widening does weaken a guard, and the deleted assertion says so in the author's own words: on a two-pin toy tree with `CI` unset and a HOME lacking the file, the parent script gives `FAILED (pin drift): 2 pin(s) checked` while the fixed script gives `OK (pin drift): 1 pin(s) checked` — the old test line `"outside CI a missing machine-local pin must stay a hard FAIL"` was removed, so if `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s playbook symlink ever breaks on the author's machine the gate now goes green with a note; nothing else depends on the old wording (only the historical record `docs/prover/2026-07-10-external-push-probe.md:52` quotes it, and gate g's known-red proof is `test_label_on_a_neighbouring_rules_line_reds`, untouched), `tests/test_traceability.py` is `180 passed` on both trees, and `git ls-files templates` shows no dotfile ships today so the dotfile skip hides nothing — but `TEST_MATRIX.md:575` still promises "strict locally", which the code no longer does, and the sibling language-rules gate treats the very same condition (layer present, file absent) as a hard fault, so the tree now holds two opposite rules for one situation.

**REFUSE** — not for the pin logic, which is proven correct and still-toothed, but because two of the demands fail on their own terms: the worktree is dirty on a protected path (`docs/PROGRESS.md`), and the commit range ships a `TEST_MATRIX.md` row that now states the opposite of the gate it pins. Both are small: decide and clean the `PROGRESS.md` modification, and restate M-154 ("noted + skipped wherever the HOME lacks the file; a present file is checked everywhere") in the same range. Re-review after that, and I'd expect ALLOW.
